text: Rosa Maria Perez, born on September 6, 1964, in the Bushwick neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City, is an American actress with roots in Puerto Rico; her mother, Lydia Pérez (née Fontañez y Reyes), was born in Humacao, Puerto Rico, and her father, Ismael Serrano, was from Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Her mother was married to a man 20 years her senior, Arturo Pérez, and had five children before becoming pregnant with Perez after an affair with Serrano. Perez was born at the now-closed Greenpoint Hospital in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, and is one of 10 children. She grew up in Bushwick with her siblings while their mother was intermittently jailed, during which time her mother gave birth to her youngest child while incarcerated. Perez was raised by an aunt and later lived in group homes and foster care in New York and Peekskill until age eight, and was legally considered a ward of the State of New York until age 12. Her mother and aunt frequently visited, and her father made an unsuccessful custody bid at one point. At age 19, Perez began her career in the early 1980s as a dancer on Soul Train; while a student at Los Angeles City College with plans to major in biochemistry, she relieved stress by attending nightclubs for ladies' night. A talent scout from Soul Train invited her to appear on the show, and she dropped out of school after becoming passionate about dancing. In 1988, at age 23, she was noticed by Spike Lee at the dance club Funky Reggae and was hired for her first major acting role in Do the Right Thing (1989). Her breakthrough came at age 24 with her portrayal of Tina in Do the Right Thing (1989), followed by White Men Can't Jump (1992). Her performance in Fearless (1993) earned her a nomination for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress, which she attended with her father. She has starred in It Could Happen to You (1994), Perdita Durango (1997), The 24 Hour Woman (1999), The Road to El Dorado (2000), Pineapple Express (2008), and Birds of Prey (2020). She provided the voice of Click, the camera, on Nick Jr.'s Go, Diego, Go! (2005–2011), and Chel, a beautiful native woman, in The Road to El Dorado (2000). She played corrupt police officer Carol Brazier in Pineapple Express (2008), co-starring Seth Rogen and James Franco. Perez earned three Primetime Emmy Award nominations for her work on In Living Color (1990–1994) and another nomination for her role in The Flight Attendant (2020–2022). She performed on Broadway in The Ritz, Frankie and Johnny in the Clair de Lune, and Fish in the Dark. She was a co-host on the ABC talk show The View during its 18th season, beginning on September 15, 2014, alongside Whoopi Goldberg, Nicolle Wallace, and Rosie O'Donnell, and left the show in July 2015. She returned to Broadway in 2015 to star in Fish in the Dark, a play written by Larry David. In 2018, she had a series regular role as Tracey Wolfe in the NBC musical drama Rise, which ran for one season. In 2020, she starred in Birds of Prey as the DC Entertainment superhero Renee Montoya / Question. In 2021, she starred in the film adaptation of the children's book series Clifford the Big Red Dog. In 2023, she had a role in season 2 of the Showtime series Your Honor. She appeared in an episode of Law & Order: Special Victims Unit in October 2009 about pedophiles' rights, where executive producer Neal Baer said the writers had her in mind for the role of a young sexual abuse victim's mother; during filming, she injured her neck and underwent surgery for a herniated disc, and one year later appeared at the White House in a wheelchair with a neck brace for a meeting with President Obama. In May 2011, she filed a lawsuit against the show's producers, claiming the injury resulted from being "recklessly pulled, grabbed, yanked, wrenched and manhandled" during filming. In June 2013, she served as grand marshal for the international Boxing Hall of Fame parade in Canastota, New York. In February 2014, she published an autobiography titled Handbook for an Unpredictable Life: How I Survived Sister Renata and My Crazy Mother, and Still Came Out Smiling..., which she also reads as an audio CD; she initially intended to write a book analyzing the causes and effects of child abuse, and found the experience cathartic after hearing responses from others. Perez is an activist for Puerto Rican rights and has suffered from high anxiety, PTSD, and depression, which have been greatly reduced through therapy. She married filmmaker and playwright Seth Zvi Rosenfeld in 1998, divorced in 2001, and married artist Eric Haze on September 15, 2013, in Las Vegas. They live in Clinton Hill, Brooklyn as of 2014. In 2021, she won the NHMC Impact Awards for Outstanding Performance in a Series.
